"NearbyIM
Linux preview {0}

Nearby text chat without an account.

Chat one to one over LAN or classic Bluetooth. Messages stay on this computer. Deleting local data removes chat history and device trust."

"Wi-Fi Direct: For Android phones and tablets, choose Wi-Fi Direct on both devices, enable reception, and search. No router is needed. Accept system connection prompts. For Windows or Linux, switch both devices to LAN and join the same Wi-Fi or hotspot. After cancellation or disconnection, both peers should tap Connect to retry.

LAN: Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi or hotspot. Enable reception and search, or enter the complete IP address and port. Chat and file transfers are end-to-end encrypted. Local history and attachments are not encrypted.

Bluetooth: Search after the other device enables reception and discovery. Follow system pairing prompts on the first connection. Remembered devices can reconnect from chat history while Bluetooth and reception remain enabled on the other device.

For the first chat, remember the device or allow this time only. Reconnection verifies the same device identity. Revoke trust in Settings.

Pending means no storage receipt has arrived. Delivered means the other device saved the message. Unconfirmed means the result is unknown. These states do not mean read.

History stays on this device. Drafts are kept when switching chats or rebuilding the interface, but may be lost when the app stops. Enable reception again after the system stops the app."

"LAN: Join the same Wi-Fi or hotspot. Enable reception and search, or enter the complete IP address and port. Chat and file transfers are end-to-end encrypted. Local history and attachments are not encrypted.

Bluetooth: Enable the adapter and the BlueZ system service. Enable reception on both devices and discoverability on the device being searched. Use system Bluetooth settings for pairing; a running desktop pairing agent is required for new devices. Paired devices and nearby search results appear in the list. Remembered devices can reconnect from history. Stopping reception keeps an established chat open.

Approve and remember a device or allow this time only. System pairing alone does not grant app trust. Reconnection verifies the same public key. Revoke trust in Settings.

Pending means no storage receipt yet; delivered means the other device saved the message; unconfirmed means the result is unknown. None means read.

History and drafts survive restarts. Enable reception again after quitting. Data is stored in XDG_DATA_HOME/wozai, or ~/.local/share/wozai by default, independently of the application folder. Private keys are stored without additional encryption and protected by owner-only file permissions. Deleting data removes history and device trust."

"LAN: Join the same Wi-Fi or hotspot on both devices. Enable reception and search, or enter the full IP address and port. Chat and file transfers are end-to-end encrypted. Local history and attachments are not encrypted.

Bluetooth: Enable reception and discoverability on the other device. Follow system pairing prompts on the first connection, using Windows Bluetooth settings if needed. Remembered devices can reconnect from chat history while Bluetooth and reception remain enabled.

For the first chat, approve and remember the device or allow this time only. Reconnection verifies the same device identity. Revoke trust in Settings.

Pending means no storage receipt yet. Delivered means the other device saved the message. Unconfirmed means the result is unknown. These states do not mean read.

History stays on this computer. Windows drafts survive conversation changes and restarts. Enable reception again after quitting.

Portable data lives in the data folder beside the app. Migration retains original files. Private identity is protected by the current Windows user and cannot automatically unlock on another user or computer. Deleting data removes history and device trust."
